title: LeBron James passes Jason Kidd for third on career assists list; can he catch Chris Paul?
content:
PHILADELPHIA — On Sunday, in a 131-124 win over the Indiana Pacers, Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James surpassed Jason Kidd to move into third place in NBA history in career assists.

With a pass to guard VJ Edgecombe, who was roaming the baseline, James recorded the 12,092 assist in his historic career. He now trails John Stockton (15,806) and Chris Paul (12,552) in the category. James is the NBA’s all-time leading scorer with 43,606 points (and counting).

“He’s got the vision and the awareness,” Sixers coach Nick Nurse said. “He’s got the size to see. He has anticipation. He knows how the defense is moving. And he throws crisp passes. Some of those are cooking out to the corner 3, so it doesn’t let the closeout get there nearly as quick.”

If James plays another season, he has a chance to pass Paul, but catching Stockton will be a tall task.

The Sixers’ win over the Pacers was their second consecutive victory, and Philly moved to 11-3 this season. The Sixers are percentage points behind the Boston Celtics atop the Eastern Conference.

Against the Pacers, James played one of his best all-around games this season. He scored 15 points, with 11 of them coming in the second half. He handed out 11 assists, and he grabbed seven rebounds.

The Sixers travel to New York, where they will face the Brooklyn Nets on Monday night.
